page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU includes a 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates that the E2s_v4 exhibits modest computational and memory performance. In multi-core processing tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, the instance scores in the bottom 10%, reflecting the physical limitation of its single-core, dual-thread layout. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 14.18 GB/sec and 11.28 GB/sec respectively, placing it in the lower tier of tested hardware. However, single-threaded performance is relatively more competitive; the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded gzip compression rates sit in the middle 50% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v4 offers a low-entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The high memory density relative to the low vCPU count makes it suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight enterprise applications. However, the poor multi-threaded performance and low memory bandwidth make it less suitable for heavy data compilation, ray tracing, or real-time large language model inference.
